title: Rigveda 7.39: To all the gods
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 7.39: To all the gods: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 7.39 is a hymn of 7 verses addressed to all the gods. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 7, the family book of Vasiṣṭha. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 520v-521r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 7.39.1-4 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 520v
translation.original_text:
1ū̱rdhvo a̱gniḥ su̍ma̱tiṁ vasvo̍ aśret pratī̱cī jū̱rṇir de̱vatā̍tim eti | bhe̱jāte̱ adrī̍ ra̱thye̍va̱ panthā̍m ṛ̱taṁ hotā̍ na iṣi̱to ya̍jāti ||
2pra vā̍vṛje supra̱yā ba̱rhir e̍ṣā̱m ā vi̱śpatī̍va̱ bīri̍ṭa iyāte | vi̱śām a̱ktor u̱ṣasa̍ḥ pū̱rvahū̍tau vā̱yuḥ pū̱ṣā sva̱staye̍ ni̱yutvā̍n ||
3jma̱yā atra̱ vasa̍vo ranta de̱vā u̱rāv a̱ntari̍kṣe marjayanta śu̱bhrāḥ | a̱rvāk pa̱tha u̍rujrayaḥ kṛṇudhva̱ṁ śrotā̍ dū̱tasya̍ ja̱gmuṣo̍ no a̱sya ||
4te hi ya̱jñeṣu̍ ya̱jñiyā̍sa̱ ūmā̍ḥ sa̱dhastha̱ṁ viśve̍ a̱bhi santi̍ de̱vāḥ | tām̐ a̍dhva̱ra u̍śa̱to ya̍kṣy agne śru̱ṣṭī bhaga̱ṁ nāsa̍tyā̱ pura̍ṁdhim ||
translation.text:
1AGNI, erect, hath shown enriching favour: the flame goes forward to the Gods' assembly. Like car-borne men the stones their path have chosen: let the priest, quickened, celebrate our worship.
2Soft to the tread, their sacred grass is scattered: these go like Kings amid the band around them, At the folks early call on Night and Morning,– Vâyu, and Pûshan with his team, to bless us.
3Here on their path the noble Gods proceeded: in the wide firmament the Beauteous decked them. Bend your way hither, ye who travel widely: hear this our envoy who hath gone to meet you.
4For they are holy aids at sacrifices: all Gods approach the place of congregation. Bring these, desirous, to our worship, Agni, swift the Nisatyas, Bhaga, and Purandhi.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 520v (numbered 41v by the scribe) (OPenn image 521, upper leaf). translation.original_ref: RV 7.39.5-7 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 4, varga 6); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 521r
translation.original_text:
5āgne̱ giro̍ di̱va ā pṛ̍thi̱vyā mi̱traṁ va̍ha̱ varu̍ṇa̱m indra̍m a̱gnim | ārya̱maṇa̱m adi̍ti̱ṁ viṣṇu̍m eṣā̱ṁ sara̍svatī ma̱ruto̍ mādayantām ||
6ra̱re ha̱vyam ma̱tibhi̍r ya̱jñiyā̍nā̱ṁ nakṣa̱t kāma̱m martyā̍nā̱m asi̍nvan | dhātā̍ ra̱yim a̍vida̱syaṁ sa̍dā̱sāṁ sa̍kṣī̱mahi̱ yujye̍bhi̱r nu de̱vaiḥ ||
7nū roda̍sī a̱bhiṣṭu̍te̱ vasi̍ṣṭhair ṛ̱tāvā̍no̱ varu̍ṇo mi̱tro a̱gniḥ | yaccha̍ntu ca̱ndrā u̍pa̱maṁ no̍ a̱rkaṁ yū̱yam pā̍ta sva̱stibhi̱ḥ sadā̍ naḥ ||
translation.text:
5Agni, to these men's hymns, from earth, from heaven, bring Mitra, Varuṇa, Indra, and Agni, And Aryaman, and Aditi, and Vishṇu. Sarasvatî be joyful, and the Maruts.
6Even as the holy wish, the gift is offered: may he, unsated, come when men desire him. Give never-failing ever-conquering riches: with Gods for our allies may we be victors.
7Now have both worlds been praised by the Vasishṭhas; and holy Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni. May they, bright Deities, make our song supremest. Preserve us evermore, ye Gods, with blessings.
